correctness.rationale: Pick gives L_P(n)=(I+B/2-1)n^2+(B/2)n+1 and L_{P×[0,k]}(n)=(kn+1)L_P(n), yielding exactly the stated cubic h* numerator 1+((k+1)(I+B)-4)t+(4kI+(2k-1)B-6k+3)t²+(k-1)It³. Independently expanded the exact cubic discriminant over disjoint chambers I=1+a,B=3+b,k=1+s and I=0,B=4+b,k=1+s. Obtained respectively 72 and 25 nonzero positive-coefficient monomials, constants 0 and 12; first chamber has coefficients 192b,288s,64a² so discriminant vanishes only at a=b=s=0 (the lone I=1,B=3,k=1 double root). The I=0,B=3 case is a simple linear polynomial. In all other degree2/3 cases discriminant is strictly positive and positive coefficients preclude nonnegative real zeros, so all zeros are simple strictly negative. Exact symbolic identities, not the 1848 sampled triples, prove the universal quantified result.
residual_risks: Only Cartesian products of full 2D lattice polygons and integer segments are proved; not all dimension-three polytopes.
Algebraic chamber positivity covers formal I>=0,B>=3; arbitrary pairs need not correspond to polygons but the stronger algebraic calculation remains valid.

originality.rationale: Universal real-rootedness for polygon-by-segment prisms is stronger than the prior log-concavity-only segment-factor theorem. Full primary text of Liu 2026, Section 2 Theorem 2.2(i), now read from arXiv article HTML, requires BOTH input h* polynomials to be real-rooted; a polygon with I=1,B=3 has h*(t)=1+t+t², not real-rooted, so that theorem does not subsume this unrestricted claim. Large-width results similarly exclude width-one prisms. Prior Wagner result under real-rooted inputs is credited.
residual_risks: An older specialized low-dimensional corollary of total-positivity or Hadamard transforms could imply the same all-polygon prism sign theorem, though none was identified in inspected primary sections.
